Title: Blood at the Root
Author: LaDarrion Williams
My Review:
Review: Blood at the Root – A Masterclass in Magic and Authenticity
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐️ (5/5)

If you are looking for a story that feels as real as your own backyard while simultaneously blowing your mind with supernatural stakes, this is it.

The Vibes: Unapologetically Us
The first thing that hits you is the authenticity. This isn't a story trying to fit Black characters into a "traditional" mold; it’s a story where the personality, the dialogue, and the rhythm of life match our actual reality. The characters felt like people I know—their humor, their protective nature, and that specific "way we move." It was refreshing to see an African American experience centered so naturally in a world of magic.

The Plot: Expect the Unexpected
I’m usually pretty good at sniffing out a plot twist a mile away, but LaDarrion Williams played me! The twists and turns in this book are top-tier. Just when I thought I had the mystery of Malik’s past and the secrets of the hidden HBCU (Caster) figured out, the rug was pulled out from under me.

The Drama: High Stakes and Heart
The drama is dialed up to 100, but it never feels forced. Whether it’s the internal friction within the magic school or the larger-than-life external threats, I was hooked from page one. It’s got:

Deep-rooted secrets that keep you turning pages.

Complex relationships that feel earned and messy.

A unique magic system that feels grounded in history. My first 5-star of the year!

Title: Breaking Lily: A Dark Psychological Romance
Author: Zaira DuMal
My Review:
Thank you to the author for the ARC in exchange for my honest review.

Breaking Lily is a dark and emotionally heavy story — and I mean dark. I went in expecting a painful journey, but this book delivers wave after wave of trauma with almost no space to breathe. Lily’s experiences are heartbreaking, and while her resilience is clear, the sheer amount of suffering she endures made the story feel more overwhelming than immersive at times.

What ultimately made this a 2-star read for me is the HEA. It doesn’t feel like true healing or safety — more like Lily ended up with the least harmful option rather than a genuinely healthy, secure love. After everything she went through, I wanted a happier ending that felt like actual peace, not just the safest corner of a traumatic world.

Readers who love extremely dark, psychologically intense stories may connect with this more than I did. But for me, the trauma overshadowed the character growth, and the resolution didn’t give Lily the kind of freedom or healing she deserved.

Babyyy, Trouble lives up to that name! And the fact that it's not just one but three of them? The Delgato brothers understood the assignment and then some.

Quick, addictive, and absolutely a must-read. If you're looking for a book that grabs you and does not let go, this is the one.

Title: Still Forever (Jennings Mafia Family #2)
Author: D. Scott
My Review:
After devouring the first book, I slid straight into this one and tore through it just the same. I love the way the Jennings brothers move, the shared qualities, the individual distinctions, the unity. Their bond is the kind of closeness I wish more melanated families had; they stayed solid, never once turning on each other or letting chaos break their circle.

Now Mr. Jaxon? He was not about to play with KD! The way he stood on business for him, even with his life possibly on the line, had me locked in. And I have to give an honorable mention to Remy — the way she stood by Jaxon, supported him, and stayed honest and intentional. Top tier.

It’s been a long time since I’ve given two back-to-back 5-star ratings in a series. Honestly, it’s only happened one other time. But this series? Yeah… It’s a solid 5 stars straight through. And now I’m running right into Judah’s story with no breaks.

Title: Legendborn (The Legendborn Cycle, #1)
Author: Tracy Deonn
My Review:
5/5 Stars – Black Girl Magic Meets Arthurian Legend in the Best Way

Legendborn by Tracy Deonn is a stunning reimagining of fantasy that unapologetically centers a Black girl’s experience in a world where she was never supposed to belong—but absolutely does. From the very first page, this book radiates with power, grief, and resilience wrapped in a story that honors ancestral strength and the richness of Southern Black culture.

Deonn weaves African American history and generational trauma into a narrative that is as magical as it is grounded. The protagonist doesn’t just face supernatural threats—she navigates spaces shaped by privilege, gatekeeping, and erasure, all while carrying the weight of her own loss. Her Blackness isn’t an afterthought—it’s a source of magic, identity, and resistance.

This is the kind of fantasy so many of us have been waiting for: where the magic isn’t just in spells and swords, but in heritage, memory, and the unbreakable ties to the ancestors who walked before us. Legendborn is more than a novel—it’s a reclamation. Bold, brilliant, and beautifully melanated. This title stands as my absolute favorite fantasy novel.

This book had me hooked from start to finish. Tiece knows how to create characters that feel real, with emotions that jump off the page. If you love a story packed with drama, passion, and characters you can’t stop thinking about, The Virgin BBW Surrogate 2 is a must-read! I’m literally about to start the third one!
